rulebook.title: UWW International Wrestling Rules (freestyle and Greco-Roman)
rulebook.text_used: equipment, mat and caution sections from secondary summaries of the UWW rules read this session (uww.org itself was not reachable); rule references are section names. Point values for cautions changed between editions, so check the current edition.

mat_m.note: the central circle is dark blue, the passivity zone orange; a summary gave the passivity band as 1.2 m, but 7 m + 2 x 1 m matches the 9 m surface

scene.text: One-piece singlet, one wrestler in red and one in blue (by draw), wrestling shoes without heels, buckles or metal, laces covered; ear guards optional for seniors; a handkerchief tucked into the singlet; no jewellery; long hair covered.

Circular 9 m competition surface on a square mat: dark-blue 7 m central circle with a 1 m starting circle in the middle, an orange 1 m passivity band around it, a protection area of a contrasting colour outside; red and blue corners diagonally opposite.
Referee on the mat wearing red and blue wristbands, a judge and a mat chairman at the table; coaches seated in the red and blue corners.

fouls.title: Greco-Roman: no holds below the waist
fouls.text: In Greco-Roman, attacking or holding the opponent below the waist and using the legs to trip, hook or block are forbidden; all holds are on the upper body.
fouls.legal: both hands are locked above the opponent's waist

fouls.title: Freestyle leg attacks are legal
fouls.text: In freestyle, grabbing the legs and tripping are allowed; a double-leg takedown is a standard legal attack.
fouls.legal: the hands are wrapped behind the opponent's legs (legal in freestyle only)

fouls.title: Illegal holds
fouls.text: Choking, the full nelson, twisting fingers or other small joints, a headlock without an arm enclosed, and bending a joint beyond its range are cautions.

fouls.title: Striking, butting, biting
fouls.text: Striking, head butting, elbowing, biting and scratching are forbidden; slamming the opponent head first into the mat is brutality.
fouls.legal: no fist or hand on the opponent's face

fouls.rule: Cautions: fleeing the mat or the hold
fouls.title: Fleeing
fouls.text: Stepping out of the circle to avoid wrestling, or fleeing a hold, is a caution with points to the opponent; a foot in the protection area in the standing position gives the opponent a point.
